Either D must be delta_{ll} tau(e_l)/dim_q, or the sentence 'Summing G^{-1} diagonal times 1/dim_q gives exactly sum 1/dim_q' must go. With inverses the entries would involve tau(sigma^{-1}) = z - h = 0.4036, not z = 0.6127. Every sibling block (def:frobenius-dual-h3, prop:frobenius-gram-matrix, rem:frobenius-gram-matrix-context) defines it without the inverse. (3) THE CASIMIR IS NOT THE CO-CASIMIR: item 2 writes C_{dim_q} = sum_{ij} (G^{-1})_{ij} b_i b_j, which is the standard Casimir Omega; thm:frobenius-codim-universal defines C_{dim_q} = sum_l p_l/(dim_q(l) tau(p_l)), and the proof of that theorem explicitly distinguishes the two ('the standard Casimir Omega = sum e_i e^i corresponds to the torus with puncture; C_{dim_q} to the torus with a dim_q-labelled puncture').
